skill.name: sent-routing-strategist
skill.description: Guides Sent channel selection, automatic routing, pinned sends, fallback behavior, rerouting, status interpretation, and evidence-based delivery diagnosis.
skill.summary: Plan and diagnose Sent message routes without unintended broadcasts, duplicate charges, or unsafe retries.
skill.author: sentdm

content.value_statement: Incorrect channel choices can cause duplicate deliveries, extra charges, failed fallback, and unsafe retries. This skill explains routing decisions and diagnoses outcomes from Sent evidence.
actual_capabilities: Distinguishes automatic routing, pinned channels, and multi-channel broadcasts.
Explains how route selection, fallback candidates, and reroutes behave.
Interprets FAILED, FILTERED, BLOCKED, SCHEDULED, and automatic channel outcomes.
Builds diagnostic sequences from message state, activities, and webhook events.
Estimates message counts and charges for multi-recipient, multi-channel sends.
Identifies when retries are appropriate, ineffective, or prohibited by consent.
limitations: Does not execute message sends or modify Sent routing rules.
Cannot access internal reason codes that Sent omits from APIs and webhooks.
Cannot guarantee a fixed channel order during automatic routing.
Does not replace consent, campaign analysis, webhook, or template-specific skills.

use_cases.title: Choose a routing mode
use_cases.description: Select automatic routing, a pinned channel, or a deliberate broadcast before implementing a send.

use_cases.title: Diagnose delivery outcomes
use_cases.description: Use message status, channel, activities, and webhook history to explain unexpected routing behavior.

use_cases.title: Review campaign cost
use_cases.description: Calculate message volume and charges before approving a multi-recipient or multi-channel campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Select a channel mode
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to send [message type] to [audience]. Explain whether I should omit channel, use automatic routing, pin one channel, or broadcast.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an unexpected outcome
prompt_templates.prompt: My message ended with status [status] and channel [channel]. Explain the likely causes, evidence to inspect, and whether I should retry.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a reroute
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this ordered activity and webhook history: [events]. Reconstruct each route attempt and identify the current logical message state.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a routing design
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this routing plan: [plan]. Check broadcast multiplication, channel constraints, fallback assumptions, retry rules, consent, status projection, and expected charges.

output_examples.input: We want WhatsApp first and SMS only if WhatsApp fails. Should we send both channel values?
output_examples.output: Use automatic routing by omitting the channel field or selecting Sent automatic routing. Supplying both channels creates two independent messages per recipient.

output_examples.input: A message shows FAILED on WhatsApp, then newer queued and delivered events on SMS.
output: The WhatsApp route failed and automatic routing reused the same message identifier.
The newer SMS delivery is the current logical outcome.
Project state by event time and keep each route attempt in the activity history.

output_examples.input: A campaign has 1,000 recipients and two channel values.
output_examples.output: The request creates 2,000 messages and potentially 2,000 charges. Confirm simultaneous delivery is intentional before sending.

best_practices: Prefer automatic routing unless compliance, contracts, or content require one channel.
Use activity history and current message state before classifying a failure as final.
Calculate recipients multiplied by channels before approving a multi-channel request.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the channel array as an ordered fallback list.
Do not retry FILTERED messages or duplicate SCHEDULED messages.
Do not infer the attempted route from the initial automatic-routing response.

faq.question: Does the channel array define fallback order?
faq.answer: No. Multiple channel values create separate messages. Use automatic routing for fallback behavior.

faq.question: When should I pin a channel?
faq.answer: Pin a channel when compliance, contract terms, or content capabilities require it. Pinned sends never cross channels.

faq.question: Can a FAILED message later deliver?
faq.answer: Yes. Automatic routing can reroute after eligible route failures and reuse the same message identifier.

faq.question: What does channel auto mean?
faq.answer: It means the message ended before a route was attempted. Review status and activities to narrow the cause.

faq.question: Should I retry a FILTERED message?
faq.answer: No. FILTERED indicates a consent or routing policy decision. Retrying can create a compliance violation.

faq.question: How do I estimate broadcast cost?
faq.answer: Multiply recipient count by channel count. Each resulting message has its own lifecycle and potential charge.
